```{r helper_func, include=FALSE}
# APA number formatter: fixed digits after the decimal, no leading zero when
# |x| < 1  (e.g. 0.234 -> .23, -0.234 -> -.23).  Reused from the main analysis.
apa_num <- function(x, digits = 2) {
  s <- ifelse(is.na(x), "",
              sprintf(paste0("%.", digits, "f"), x))
  sub("^(-?)0\\.", "\\1.", s)
}

std_to_ref <- function(x, ref, sign = 1) {
  m  <- mean(ref, na.rm = TRUE)
  s  <- sd(ref,   na.rm = TRUE)
  sign * (x - m) / s
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# build_cor_table(df, vars, labels)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Returns a tibble that renders as a lower-triangular correlation matrix with
# APA-formatted cells and superscript significance signs.  Each numeric cell
# is wrapped in the same 5em fixed-width block used by the regression tables,
# so decimals line up across rows AND across columns:
#
#     [   .23<sup>*</sup>  ]
#     [ -.45<sup>***</sup> ]
#     [   .01              ]
#
# * Pearson r via pairwise-complete `cor.test`.
# * sig sign scheme (matches the regression tables):
#     † p < .10   * p < .05   ** p < .01   *** p < .001
# * Diagonal shows an em-dash; upper triangle is left blank.
build_cor_table <- function(df, vars, labels, digits = 2,
                             cell_width = "4em") {

  pad_cell <- function(num_str, sig_str = "") {
    paste0(
      "<span style='display:inline-block;width:", cell_width,
      ";text-align:right'>",
      num_str,
      "<span style='display:inline-block;min-width:1.4em;text-align:left'>",
      sig_str,
      "</span></span>"
    )
  }

  sig_sup <- function(p) dplyr::case_when(
    is.na(p) ~ "",
    p < 0.001 ~ "<sup>***</sup>",
    p < 0.01  ~ "<sup>**</sup>",
    p < 0.05  ~ "<sup>*</sup>",
    p < 0.10  ~ "<sup>&dagger;</sup>",
    TRUE      ~ ""
  )

  x <- df %>% dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(vars)) %>% as.matrix()
  n <- length(vars)
  cells <- matrix("", n, n, dimnames = list(labels, labels))

  for (i in seq_len(n)) {
    for (j in seq_len(n)) {
      if (j > i) {
        cells[i, j] <- ""              # blank upper triangle
      } else if (i == j) {
        cells[i, j] <- pad_cell("—")   # diagonal
      } else {
        pair <- na.omit(x[, c(i, j)])
        if (nrow(pair) < 3) {
          cells[i, j] <- pad_cell("")
        } else {
          ct <- suppressWarnings(cor.test(pair[, 1], pair[, 2]))
          cells[i, j] <- pad_cell(apa_num(ct$estimate, digits),
                                  sig_sup(ct$p.value))
        }
      }
    }
  }

  tibble::as_tibble(cells, rownames = "Variable")
}

# ---- Fixed-width right-aligned spans so decimals column-align across rows ----
num_cell <- function(x, w = "3.5em")
  paste0("<span style='display:inline-block;width:", w,
         ";text-align:right'>", x, "</span>")

n_cell <- function(n, w = "3.5em")
  paste0("<span style='display:inline-block;width:", w,
         ";text-align:right'>", format(n, big.mark = ","), "</span>")

range_cell <- function(lo, hi) {
  if (is.na(lo) || is.na(hi)) return("")
  paste0(num_cell(apa_num(lo)), " – ", num_cell(apa_num(hi)))
}

# ---- Build one row of stats from a (var, label, df, theo_lo, theo_hi) ----
compute_row <- function(var, label, df, theo_lo, theo_hi) {
  x <- as.numeric(df[[var]])
  x <- x[!is.na(x)]
  tibble::tibble(
    Variable            = label,
    N                   = n_cell(length(x)),
    Mean                = num_cell(apa_num(mean(x))),
    Median              = num_cell(apa_num(median(x))),
    SD                  = num_cell(apa_num(sd(x))),
    `Theoretical range` = range_cell(theo_lo, theo_hi),
    `Observed range`    = range_cell(min(x), max(x))
  )
}
```

# Table S1. Descriptive statistics for Outcome Variables
```{r outcome_desp}
# Order of time points: baseline block, then 3m FU block, then 20m FU block.
# Theoretical range reported only for the scale-bounded measures (K6, Cantril
# ladder, FCS, K10, PHQ-9, GAD-7, subjective peacefulness, positive affect);
# left blank for the composite z-score indices and the two binary baseline
# indicators.
#
# Baseline block: pulled from C2TB_bsl (the baseline analysis file). Note:
# baseline Ns here reflect the full baseline sample, which can differ from
# the Ns for the same `*_bsl` columns in C2TB_stfu_wins (restricted to HHs
# that reached the 3m FU).
# 3m FU block:    C2TB_stfu_wins.
# 20m FU block:   C2TB_enl_wins.

# ---- Variable specification ----
# wave_set: "bsl" => baseline block only
#           "fu"  => appears in BOTH 3m FU and 20m FU blocks
desc_vars <- tibble::tribble(
  ~var,                   ~label,                               ~wave_set, ~theo_lo, ~theo_hi,
  "kessler_6_bsl",        "Kessler-6",                          "bsl",      0,        24,
  "cantrils_bsl",         "Global life satisfaction",          "bsl",      1,        10,
  "bsl_fambus",           "Household owns family business",     "bsl",      NA,       NA,
  "bsl_outhh_empl",       "Household member works for payment", "bsl",      NA,       NA,
  "fcs_bsl",              "Food consumption score",             "bsl",      0,        112,
  "psych_distress_index", "Psychological distress index",       "fu",       NA,       NA,
  "kessler_10",           "Kessler-10",                         "fu",       0,        40,
  "phq_total_score",      "PHQ-9",                              "fu",       0,        27,
  "gad_total_score",      "GAD-7",                              "fu",       0,        21,
  "psych_well_being_z",   "Psychological well-being index",       "fu",       NA,       NA,
  "cantrils",             "Global life satisfaction",          "fu",       1,        10,
  "subj_peace",           "Subjective peacefulness",            "fu",       1,        10,
  "positive_affect",      "Positive affect",                    "fu",       0,        1,
  "econ_activity_index",  "Economic activity index",            "fu",       NA,       NA,
  "labor_supply_index",   "Labor supply index",                 "fu",       NA,       NA,
  "investment_index",     "Investment index",                   "fu",       NA,       NA,
  "econ_expansion_index", "Economic expansion index",           "fu",       NA,       NA,
  "fcs",                  "Food consumption score",             "fu",       0,        112
)

bsl_idx <- which(desc_vars$wave_set == "bsl")
fu_idx  <- which(desc_vars$wave_set == "fu")

rows_bsl <- purrr::map_dfr(bsl_idx, function(i) {
  r <- desc_vars[i, ]
  compute_row(r$var, r$label, C2TB_bsl, r$theo_lo, r$theo_hi)
})
rows_stfu <- purrr::map_dfr(fu_idx, function(i) {
  r <- desc_vars[i, ]
  compute_row(r$var, r$label, C2TB_stfu_wins, r$theo_lo, r$theo_hi)
})
rows_enl <- purrr::map_dfr(fu_idx, function(i) {
  r <- desc_vars[i, ]
  compute_row(r$var, r$label, C2TB_enl_wins,  r$theo_lo, r$theo_hi)
})

desc_tbl <- dplyr::bind_rows(rows_bsl, rows_stfu, rows_enl)

n_bsl <- nrow(rows_bsl)
n_fu  <- nrow(rows_stfu)   # same as nrow(rows_enl)

tableS1_kbl <-
  kableExtra::kbl(
    desc_tbl,
    align   = "lcccccc",
    escape  = FALSE
  ) %>%
  kableExtra::pack_rows("Baseline",            1,                  n_bsl,              bold = TRUE) %>%
  kableExtra::pack_rows("3 month post-treatment",   n_bsl + 1,          n_bsl + n_fu,       bold = TRUE) %>%
  kableExtra::pack_rows("20 month post-treatment",  n_bsl + n_fu + 1,   n_bsl + 2 * n_fu,   bold = TRUE) %>%
  kableExtra::kable_styling(full_width = FALSE,
                             bootstrap_options = c("hover", "condensed"))

# Render inline (knitted HTML output + interactive session)
tableS1_kbl
```

# Table S2. Correlations among primary outcomes at 3m FU and 20m FU

Four primary outcomes at each of two follow-ups are jointly correlated:
psychological distress (`psych_distress_index`), psychological well-being
(`psych_well_being_z`), economic activity (`econ_activity_index`), and
food security (`fcs`), each measured at the 3-month follow-up (`_stfu`)
and the 20-month follow-up (`_enl`). Correlations are Pearson
product-moment coefficients computed on pairwise-complete cases;
significance signs use the same scheme as the regression tables
(`&dagger; p < .10, * p < .05, ** p < .01, *** p < .001`).

```{r cor_dv_setup, include = FALSE}
# Wide frame of the 4 primary DVs at both follow-ups, joined on hhid.
# `full_join` keeps every household that appears at either follow-up so no
# pair is dropped unnecessarily; `cor.test` uses pairwise-complete cases
# inside `build_cor_table`, so per-cell N will vary.
cor_wide <-
  C2TB_stfu_wins %>%
  dplyr::select(hhid,
                distress_stfu  = psych_distress_index,
                wellbeing_stfu = psych_well_being_z,
                econ_stfu      = econ_activity_index,
                fcs_stfu       = fcs) %>%
  dplyr::full_join(
    C2TB_enl_wins %>%
      dplyr::select(hhid,
                    distress_enl  = psych_distress_index,
                    wellbeing_enl = psych_well_being_z,
                    econ_enl      = econ_activity_index,
                    fcs_enl       = fcs),
    by = "hhid"
  )

dv_vars_wide <- c("distress_stfu",  "wellbeing_stfu", "econ_stfu",  "fcs_stfu",
                  "distress_enl",   "wellbeing_enl",  "econ_enl",   "fcs_enl")

# Two-line labels via <br>: DV name on line 1, timepoint on line 2.
dv_labels_wide <- c(
  "Psychological distress<br><em>(3m FU)</em>",
  "Psychological well-being<br><em>(3m FU)</em>",
  "Economic activity<br><em>(3m FU)</em>",
  "Food security<br><em>(3m FU)</em>",
  "Psychological distress<br><em>(20m FU)</em>",
  "Psychological well-being<br><em>(20m FU)</em>",
  "Economic activity<br><em>(20m FU)</em>",
  "Food security<br><em>(20m FU)</em>"
)
```

```{r cor_combined}
build_cor_table(cor_wide, dv_vars_wide, dv_labels_wide,
                cell_width = "4em") %>%
  kbl(align   = "lcccccccc",
      escape  = FALSE,
      caption = "Table S1. Correlations among primary outcomes at 3m FU and 20m FU.") %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE,
                bootstrap_options = c("hover", "condensed")) %>%
  footnote(general       = "&dagger; p < .10, * p < .05, ** p < .01, *** p < .001. Pearson correlations on pairwise-complete cases; per-cell N varies with joint missingness.",
           general_title = "Note.",
           escape        = FALSE,
           footnote_as_chunk = TRUE)
```

# Table S3. Psychosocial Indices Description

```{r mech_desp}
# One row per psychosocial-mechanism index.
# Columns: Index (pretty name), Scaling, Sample item, Cronbach's alpha,
# Composite score creation.
#
# The item lists mirror Matt's cleaning script (05_merge_and_indices.do)
# so alpha is computed on the raw items that go into each composite.
# `psych::alpha(..., check.keys = TRUE)` auto-detects reverse-scored items,
# which matches Matt's recodes for the communication, grit, self-control
# and mind_along items.

# --- Item lists per index (raw variable names in C2TB_stfu_wins) ---
mech_items <- list(
  optimistic_future      = c("future_relative_ses", "child_aspirations",
                             "future_life_sat"),
  social_worth =           c("worth_family", "worth_community",
                             "worth_famresp", "worth_comresp",
                             "relative_ses"),   # 4 "worth" items + MacArthur ladder
  self_efficacy          = c("eff_solveprob_hard", "eff_opposes", "eff_accomgoal",
                             "eff_confident", "eff_resourceful",
                             "eff_solveprob_tryhard", "eff_remaincalm",
                             "eff_confrontprob", "eff_trouble", "eff_handle"),
  spousal_communication  = c("freq_disc_day", "freq_disc_worries",
                             "freq_disc_decision", "freq_part_listens",
                             "freq_part_thanks", "freq_part_humiliates",
                             "freq_rslv_calmly", "freq_rslv_eachother",
                             "freq_rslv_yelling", "freq_rslv_threats"),
  meta_cognitive         = c("mind_calm", "mind_reflect", "mind_emotions",
                             "mind_interact", "mind_understand", "mind_along",
                             "goals_challenges"),
  social_inclusion       = c("close_household", "close_spouse", "close_community",
                             "loneliness", "social_excluded_rev_z",
                             "harassment_rev_z"),
  grit                   = c("grit_newidea", "grit_setback", "grit_setgoal",
                             "grit_hardwork", "grit_focus", "grit_finishall",
                             "grit_interest", "grit_diligent", "grit_obsessed",
                             "grit_setbacks", "grit_achievement"),
  self_control           = c("sc1_habits", "sc2_distracted", "sc3_inappropriate",
                             "sc4_refuse", "sc5_resist", "sc6_selfdiscipline",
                             "sc7_pleasure", "sc8_feelgood", "sc9_stop",
                             "sc10_alternatives")
)


# --- Sanity check: every item in mech_items must exist in C2TB_stfu_wins ---
mech_items_all     <- unique(unlist(mech_items))
mech_items_missing <- setdiff(mech_items_all, names(C2TB_stfu_wins))

if (length(mech_items_missing) > 0) {
  cat("MISSING from C2TB_stfu_wins (", length(mech_items_missing), " item(s)):\n", sep = "")
  cat(paste0("  - ", mech_items_missing), sep = "\n")
  cat("\nPer-index breakdown:\n")
  for (idx in names(mech_items)) {
    bad <- setdiff(mech_items[[idx]], names(C2TB_stfu_wins))
    if (length(bad) > 0) {
      cat(sprintf("  %-22s %s\n", paste0(idx, ":"),
                  paste(bad, collapse = ", ")))
    }
  }
  stop("Fix mech_items (or add the missing columns to C2TB_stfu_wins) ",
       "before computing alpha.")
} else {
  cat("All ", length(mech_items_all), " items present in C2TB_stfu_wins.\n", sep = "")
}

# --- Cronbach's alpha per entry in mech_items ---
# `psych::alpha(..., check.keys = TRUE)` auto-reverses items whose correlation
# with the composite is negative — matches Matt's reverse-coding of the
# humiliation/yelling/threats, grit, self-control, and mind_along items.
for (idx in names(mech_items)) {
  items <- mech_items[[idx]]
  mat   <- as.data.frame(C2TB_stfu_wins[, items, drop = FALSE])
  mat[] <- lapply(mat, as.numeric)
  a <- suppressMessages(suppressWarnings(
    psych::alpha(mat, check.keys = TRUE, warnings = FALSE)
  ))
  cat(sprintf("%-24s alpha = %.3f   (k = %d items, n = %d complete cases)\n",
              paste0(idx, ":"),
              as.numeric(a$total["raw_alpha"]),
              length(items),
              sum(complete.cases(mat))))
}

C2TB_stfu_wins %>%
  dplyr::select(close_household, close_spouse, close_community,
                             loneliness) %>%
  alpha()
```
